gap: No result ChatGPT got that I opened states that the makers' headline numbers are not the same measurement: Redragon, Royal Kludge, Epomaker and Gamakay's NS68 quote "0.125 ms", which is only 1 ÷ 8,000 Hz; Gamakay's NS75 and TK75HE V2 (0.06 ms) and MCHOSE (0.1 ms) quote figures shorter than that report gap; and the rapid trigger figure runs from Redragon's 0.1 mm setting step, with Redragon's own tolerance caveat, to 0.005 mm "accuracy" at ATK and Gamakay, while MonsGeek says 0.01 mm holds for only six switches.
standout_why: I opened five of the results: mkbguide.com (cited), hlplanet.com (cited), mechanicalkeyboard.net best-budget (cited), gamepadsquire.com (cited) and setupinsider.com; the other results were not opened, so the claim covers only these five. MKB Guide gives polling rate by connection mode and nothing on rapid trigger step, scan rate or latency. HLPlanet gives prices and scattered polling figures, with no rapid trigger step or scan rate for any board under $100. mechanicalkeyboard.net already says 0.125 ms is a reporting interval and not end-to-end latency, so that part is not new. GamepadSquire lists advertised precision (0.01 / 0.005 mm) and scan rates (128 / 160 / 256 kHz) as spec-sheet values without saying they are on different bases. SetupInsider notes the K707 HE's 0.1 mm steps but not Redragon's tolerance footnote. None of the five has Redragon's tolerance footnote, MonsGeek's six-switch limit, the latency claims that sit below the 8,000 Hz report gap, or the 16K to 256K scan-rate spread side by side. I found no independent measurement, so the finding is a decoding of maker claims.
decides: It mostly confirms ChatGPT's own caveat and does not crown a winner on speed: once the claims are put on one basis, every candidate reports to the PC at most every 0.125 ms on a cable, and the latency, scan-rate and "accuracy" figures cannot rank them. Three things do separate them. (1) Redragon K707 HE ($49.99) is the only one whose maker states a 0.1 mm step; the others state 0.01 mm or finer. (2) 8,000 Hz without a cable: Gamakay's NS75 blog says "true wired 8000 Hz" and gives no 2.4 GHz figure, so our NS75 row should claim 8K for wired only; MonsGeek states 8K on wired or 2.4G for the FUN60 Ultra, but monsgeek.com showed it unavailable with a waitlist on 2026-11-21; MKB Guide states 8K on USB and 2.4 GHz for the Epomaker HE65 V2 TMR ($59.99). (3) For a wired-only buyer, the $36.79 to $42.49 boards (Gamakay NS68, MCHOSE Ace 60 Pro, Epomaker HE68 Lite) carry the same paper claims as the $60 to $90 ones, so layout and wireless decide the spend. Our NS75 can honestly take the "75% with knob and three connection modes" segment, not "fastest".
